official.deadline_note: The online application portal (www.eastwestcenter.org/applyGDF) closes at 11:59 PM Hawai'i Standard Time on December 1. Official transcripts, official English test scores, and three letters of reference must be RECEIVED by January 10; the University of Hawai'i admission application is also due December 1 and must be completed (including any departmental application) by January 10.
official.application_cycle: Current competition opens 16 August 2026 and closes 1 December 2026 for the fellowship year beginning August 2027; results are emailed in early April
official.status_note: The EWC Apply page lists an opening date of 16 August 2026 and a closing date of 1 December 2026, so the competition is open as of verification; one paragraph of that page still carries older 'academic year 2026-2027 competition' wording.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Full-time graduate tuition and fees up to the equivalent of the general tuition charged for post-baccalaureate students at the University of Hawai'i at Mānoa toward master's or doctoral studies.
benefits: Full-time graduate tuition and fees up to the equivalent of the general tuition charged for post-baccalaureate students at UHM toward master's or doctoral studies
Housing in an East-West Center residence hall for the academic year, based on single occupancy
A stipend to partially cover food and incidental expenses
Competitive funding for field study and conference presentations during the fellow's period of study, subject to funding availability
Automatic consideration for EWC Alumni and Foundation scholarships, which may provide limited supplemental support to finalists with demonstrated financial need
eligibility: Citizens or permanent residents of the United States, or citizens of listed Pacific, Southeast Asian, South Asian and East Asian countries (including China, India, Indonesia, Japan, Korea, Malaysia, Philippines, Russia, Taiwan, Thailand, Vietnam, Australia and New Zealand)
A 4-year bachelor's degree or equivalent from an accredited US institution or recognized institution abroad obtained before the award begins
Minimum grade point average of 3.0 (4.0=A) or equivalent in the last four semesters or six quarters of the undergraduate record and in all post-baccalaureate work
Admission to a University of Hawai'i at Mānoa graduate degree program (separate application due December 1)

Priority to applicants with a demonstrated commitment to the goals, objectives, and priorities of the East-West Center, including advancement of economic security for a more innovative, resilient, sustainable, secure, and prosperous Indo-Pacific region
requirements: Online application submitted at www.eastwestcenter.org/applyGDF by December 1
Curriculum vitae or resume uploaded by December 1
Application Acknowledgment from the University of Hawai'i (screenshot or PDF) uploaded by December 1 for applicants applying to UH simultaneously
Passport biodata page uploaded by December 1 (international students only)

Three letters of reference received by January 10, two addressing academic abilities and professional objectives and one reflecting community service, civic engagement, or extra-curricular involvement
Official transcripts from each college or university attended received by January 10
Official IELTS, DUOLINGO, or TOEFL score reported directly by the testing service by January 10 where proof of English proficiency is required
documents: University of Hawai'i Application Acknowledgment (screenshot or PDF)
Official transcripts from every college or university attended
Official IELTS, DUOLINGO, or TOEFL score report sent by the testing service
Three letters of reference (two academic/professional, one civic engagement) on the EWC-provided reference forms
selection_criteria: Awarded annually in an international competition
Priority to applicants with demonstrated commitment to EWC goals, objectives and priorities, including Indo-Pacific economic security
Academic record, evidenced by transcripts (minimum 3.0 GPA) and the two academic/professional letters of reference
Involvement in community service, civic engagement, or extra-curricular activities, evidenced by the third letter
Field of study relevant to the goals and objectives of the East-West Center
coverage: General tuition and fees for University of Hawai'i at Mānoa graduate programs
Housing in an East-West Center dormitory for the academic year (single occupancy)
Partial stipend toward food and incidental expenses
The GDF provisions approximate $22,000 (less applicable taxes) per year
All other costs of study and residence in Hawai'i remain the responsibility of the awardee
application_method: Complete the online application at www.eastwestcenter.org/applyGDF by December 1
Submit a separate graduate admission application to the University of Hawai'i at Mānoa by December 1
Forward the EWC Letter of Reference link to three referees so their letters arrive by January 10
Arrange official transcripts and English test scores to reach EWC directly by January 10
official.application_route: Apply online at www.eastwestcenter.org/applyGDF by December 1 and separately submit a UH Mānoa graduate admission application by December 1 (completed, with departmental materials, by January 10).
official.citizenship_residency: Open to citizens or permanent residents of the United States and to citizens of listed Pacific, Southeast Asian, South Asian and East Asian countries; permanent residency outside these groups is not sufficient
official.international_eligibility: Yes - citizens of the listed Asia-Pacific countries are eligible. Degree fellows who are not US citizens or permanent residents must come on a J-1 Exchange Visitor visa and are subject to a two-year home-country physical presence requirement after program completion; post-completion academic training is available except to ADB-JSP scholars.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Fields of study relevant to the goals and objectives of the East-West Center, pursued through a UH Mānoa graduate program; certain professional programs (e.g. Architecture, DNP, JD, LLM, MAcc, MBA, MD, MSN) are not fully covered by the general tuition provision
official.duration: Granted one academic year (fall and spring semesters) at a time and renewable for a second academic year, subject to funding availability and satisfactory progress; an individual may receive the GDF for no more than two academic years total
official.description: The East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship provides master's and doctoral degree funding for graduate students from Asia, the Pacific, and the United States to pursue graduate study at the University of Hawai'i at Mānoa while participating in the Center's educational, cultural, residential community-building, and leadership development programs. The fellowship covers UHM graduate tuition and fees, single-occupancy housing in an East-West Center residence hall, and a stipend that partially covers food and incidental expenses.
official.region: Honolulu, Hawai'i, United States (University of Hawai'i at Mānoa)
official.program_type: Graduate degree fellowship (master's and doctoral) attached to University of Hawai'i at Mānoa admission
official.english_requirement: Where proof of English proficiency is required, the Center requires a minimum TOEFL score of 79, DUOLINGO score of 95, or total band 6.5 on the IELTS academic test, reported by the testing service by January 10. UH grants an exception only if you studied in a country where English is the first language and received your degree there within the past five years.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a fully tuition-and-housing-covered path into a UH Mānoa master's or PhD, but plan on self-funding a meaningful slice of living costs: the food and incidental stipend is partial and EWC states all other Hawai'i expenses are yours. The real deadline work is front-loaded - your EWC portal application and your UH admission application must both be in by 1 December, and transcripts, scores and all three reference letters only need to arrive by 10 January. International applicants should factor the J-1 two-year home-residence rule into any post-graduation plan before applying.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mid-career or early-career researchers and postgraduates from the Asia-Pacific or the US with Indo-Pacific-focused study goals who are comfortable living in a residential fellowship community in Honolulu.
application_readiness_checklist: Create the EWC portal account well before 1 December and confirm you can upload files in the required formats
Submit the UH Mānoa graduate admission application early enough to receive the Application Acknowledgment email, then screenshot it for the EWC upload
Brief your three referees immediately: two academic/professional letters and one on community service or civic engagement, using the specific EWC forms
Book your IELTS/TOEFL/DUOLINGO early enough that official scores can be sent to EWC by 10 January
Request official transcripts from every institution attended now, including graduate-level coursework
Check your target UH department for its own supplemental application, GRE/GMAT, or portfolio requirements, and finish it before 10 January
common_rejection_risks: Missing reference letters: EWC states an application will not be reviewed without all three letters, regardless of the rest of its strength
A UH departmental application left incomplete past 10 January, which lets the department miss the admission decision and drops the application from the eligible pool
English test scores taken too late to reach EWC directly from the test service by 10 January
Choosing a professional program (MBA, MAcc, JD, LLM, MD, DNP, MSN, Architecture) without a plan for the tuition differential the fellowship does not cover
Applying from a non-eligible country or as a permanent resident of an eligible country without its citizenship
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Food and incidental expenses beyond the partial stipend, international airfare to and from Honolulu, professional-program tuition differentials, books and supplies, health insurance and personal costs. EWC states all other costs related to study and residence in Hawai'i are the awardee's responsibility and directs applicants to UH cost-of-education estimates; the award also explicitly provides no spousal or dependent support.
document_audit: Transcripts must be official and cover every institution attended, not just your degree-granting university
The two reference types matter: referees receive different EWC forms for the academic/professional letter and the civic-engagement letter, so send each referee the correct link
The UH Application Acknowledgment must be uploaded with the EWC application by 1 December; a completed UH application without the uploaded acknowledgment does not count
English scores must come directly from the testing service - screenshots or self-reported scores are not accepted by the 10 January cutoff
International applicants add only the passport biodata page; no extra financial statements are listed by EWC, but budget proof-of-funds questions at the J-1 visa stage
alerts: The portal closes at 11:59 PM Hawai'i Standard Time on 1 December - applicants in Asia and the Pacific should not treat the end of 1 December local time as the cutoff
The award cannot be deferred: if you cannot be in residence in Honolulu from mid-August, you must reapply in a later cycle
New fellows must arrive alone for the first semester, and fellows with children under 18 must live off-campus, which strains the partial stipend in Honolulu's housing market
Non-US fellows accept a two-year home-country physical presence obligation under the J-1 program before returning on H/F visas
Second-year renewal depends on funding availability and satisfactory academic and EWC program progress, so treat year two as conditional
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the EWC online application plus the UH admission application by 1 December, track the completeness email, and let transcripts, scores and reference letters land by 10 January; EWC emails the decision in early April.
